subject: feeding environment variables into ggplot functions

messages.author: b8d025f1c60d2466
messages.subject: feeding environment variables into ggplot functions
parts:
Dear list—

I was wondering if it is possible to have the aes function to take
variables from a higher function environment as an argument. This
question arose when I was trying to produce a series of plots in batch
from the same data frame, with the value of one of the aesthetics
becoming an external variable in a loop.

Take the following example:

df <- data.frame (a = rnorm (10, 0, 1), b = rnorm (10, 0, 10), c =
rnorm (10, 10, 5), y = 1:10)

Here, I would like to produce 3 scatterplots of a, b and c plotted
against y in one full swing. Ideally, something like this would do the
trick IF the aes function would be able to take in the variable 'var'
from the sapply function environment:

sapply (letters[1:3], function (var)
{
pdf (paste (var, ".pdf", sep = ""))
ggplot (df, aes (var, y)) +
geom_point ()
dev.off ()
})

Is there a way to feed external environment variables into ggplot functions?

Thanking you in advance,
—Gil

messages.subject: Re: feeding environment variables into ggplot functions

Thanks Hadley!

For future reference, here's the bit code producing the intended
result in my example:

p <- ggplot (df, aes_string (x = var, y = "y")) +
geom_point ()
print (p)
dev.off ()
})
